No new code is submitted. Let `G_*` be the independently accepted `1040×n` RS–affine generator, with columns `z_v∈V=F_2^1040`. Its columns span `V`, and the constant-message vector `j` satisfies `j·z_v=1` for every coordinate `v`.

Deterministically scan the base coordinates in their fixed order, retaining the first column independent of those already retained. This produces indices `b_1,…,b_1040` whose columns form an ordered basis `P=[z_{b_1}|…|z_{b_1040}]`.

Given any deterministic column stream `g_1,…,g_n∈V`, compute `a_q=P^{-1}g_q`. On the explicit complete graph `K_n` on the base-coordinate indices, represent `g_q` by visiting the basis vertices in the support of `a_q`, in increasing order. If the support is empty, use `(b_1,b_2,b_1,b_2)`; if it is a singleton `{b_i}`, use `(b_i,b_h,b_i,b_h,b_i)` for the first `h≠i`. These exceptional walks have the same XOR and parity as the desired support. Every walk therefore has at most 1040 vertex visits, its visited-label XOR is exactly `g_q`, and its visit parity is `j·g_q`.

If, in addition, `|Σ_q(-1)^(x·g_q)|≤2^21` for every nonzero `x∈V`, then the matrix whose `q`th column is `(g_q,1)` generates a binary `[2^30,1041,≥535822336]` code. No stream satisfying these inequalities is supplied here, so this is an explicitness compiler and obstruction, not a leaderboard construction.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Parameterized emitter only; no qualifying parameter is supplied. Given a deterministic stream `Col` producing `g_q∈F_2^1040` for `q=0,…,n−1`, emit the 1041-bit column `(g_q,1)`. If instead given a path stream, initialize `g_q=0`, compute each visited base column by `G_*[(j,i),(a,y)]=h_y(α^i a^j)`, XOR it into `g_q`, and then emit `(g_q,1)`. The basis-walk compiler converts a `Col` stream into paths by the deterministic scan and inversion described above.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: If the complete column stream takes `P(n)` bit operations, direct matrix emission takes at most `P(n)+1041n` operations. If a path stream takes `Q(n)` operations and has `L` total visits, emission takes less than `Q(n)+2^25 L+1041n` bit operations. Compiling a column stream into the at-most-1040-visit basis walks takes less than `P(n)+2^27 n` bit operations.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: A base entry needs at most 15 naive degree-16 field multiplications plus fewer than 64 affine-bit operations; with fewer than 1024 bit operations per multiplication, this is below `2^14` operations. Hence one full 1040-bit base column costs below `2^25` operations, proving the path-emitter bound. Computing all base columns for the deterministic basis scan costs below `2^25 n`; elimination and all `P^{-1}g_q` products cost below `2^22 n` each, inversion costs polynomially fewer than this target-scale bound, and descriptor output costs below `2^16 n`. Their sum is below `2^27 n`. Thus polynomial-time input streams give polynomial-time full-matrix output. Since no Fourier-qualified input stream is supplied, this runtime theorem does not constitute a candidate.

proof_markdown:
## Basis-walk explicitness theorem

Let `V=F_2^1040`, and let `z_1,…,z_n` be the columns of the accepted RS–affine generator. Its rank is 1040, so these columns span `V`. The message `j` for the constant polynomial 1 satisfies `j·z_v=1` for every `v`.

### Deterministic basis and walk compilation

Scan the columns in their fixed order and retain a column precisely when Gaussian reduction finds it independent of the retained set. Full column rank guarantees termination with an ordered basis `P=[z_{b_1}|…|z_{b_1040}]`. This is deterministic polynomial-time linear algebra on an explicit matrix.

For any desired column `g`, set `a=P^{-1}g`. If at least two entries of `a` are one, visit their basis vertices in increasing order in `K_n`. They are distinct, so this is a valid walk. The displayed four- and five-visit replacements handle zero and singleton supports without loops. In every case the XOR of visited labels is `g`. Moreover, each basis label has `j`-value one, so the visit count modulo two is `Σ_i a_i=j·g`; the exceptional replacements preserve this parity. The walk uses at most 1040 visits.

Conversely, a path indexer computes its lifted column by XORing the explicitly computable labels of its visited vertices. Thus polynomial-time column streams and polynomial-total-visit path streams reduce to one another with the stated polynomial overhead.

### Fourier criterion, rank, and distance

For a column stream `g_q`, put `S_x=Σ_q(-1)^(x·g_q)`. The word generated by `(x,b)∈V×F_2` from the matrix with columns `(g_q,1)` has signed sum `(-1)^bS_x` and weight `(n−(-1)^bS_x)/2`.

Suppose `|S_x|≤T` for every nonzero `x`. A nonzero kernel vector would give `S_x=n`, and a core word equal to `1^n` would give `S_x=−n`; both contradict `T<n`. Hence the first 1040 rows have full rank and do not contain the appended constant row. The augmented code therefore has dimension 1041. Every message with `x≠0` has weight at least `(n−T)/2=D`, while `(0,1)` has weight `n`. This proves the target for every nonzero word.

Conversely, if the constant augmentation has dimension 1041 and minimum distance at least `D`, then for each nonzero `x`, both the core word and its complement are nonzero and have weight at least `D`. Therefore its weight lies in `[D,n−D]`, equivalently `|S_x|≤n−2D=T`. Thus the Fourier condition is necessary and sufficient.

Writing `V=U⊕<j>`, split indices according to `j·g_q`. For `u∈U`, the character sums of `u` and `u+j` are `A_u+B_u` and `A_u−B_u`; `max(|A+B|,|A−B|)=|A|+|B|`. This is exactly the upstream parity-split system.

### Spectral obstruction

The host `K_n` has normalized nonprincipal eigenvalue magnitude `1/(n−1)`. Nevertheless, taking the four-visit zero walk for every output produces `g_q=0` and character sums `n`. Therefore host expansion and a short-walk bound alone cannot certify a sparse schedule. All bias reduction must come from a proved property of the actual deterministic walk distribution.

No Fourier-qualified column stream or path family is supplied. The result is therefore a proved explicitness compiler and obstruction, not a leaderboard construction.

proof_steps.proof: The accepted generator has row and column rank 1040. Its constant-polynomial row is one on every coordinate, so the corresponding message `j` evaluates to one on every column.
proof_steps.statement: The explicit base columns span `F_2^1040` and all lie in the affine hyperplane `j·z=1`.

proof_steps.proof: Lexicographic incremental Gaussian elimination retains exactly the first 1040 independent columns. Spanning guarantees success, and direct base-column evaluation plus at most 1040 pivots per column gives polynomial runtime.
proof_steps.statement: An ordered basis of base columns is recoverable deterministically without a construction search.

proof_steps.proof: Expand `g=P a`. Visiting the support basis vertices XORs to `g`; the zero and singleton replacement walks add each auxiliary label an even number of times. Since every basis label has `j`-value one, visit parity equals `j·g`.
proof_steps.statement: Every column is represented by a valid explicit `K_n` walk with at most 1040 visits and the correct parity.

proof_steps.proof: XOR the directly computed base labels along each indexed path. Polynomial descriptor time and polynomial total visits give a polynomial-time column stream and full generator emitter.
proof_steps.statement: Every explicit polynomial-total-visit path family yields an explicit column stream with polynomial overhead.

proof_steps.proof: Use `wt=(n−signed-sum)/2`. The absolute bound covers a word and its complement, rules out a kernel and the all-one core word, and proves rank 1041 after augmentation. The reverse implication follows by applying the distance bound to both cosets.
proof_steps.statement: The universal `2^21` Fourier bound is equivalent to a rank-1041 all-one augmentation meeting the target.

proof_steps.proof: The characters `u` and `u+j` have sums `A_u+B_u` and `A_u−B_u`, while `j` measures the parity-class size difference. Apply `max(|A+B|,|A−B|)=|A|+|B|`.
proof_steps.statement: The compiler’s global Fourier test exactly instantiates the upstream parity-split acceptance interface.

proof_steps.proof: `K_n` has normalized nonprincipal eigenvalue `−1/(n−1)`, but repeating the valid zero-XOR walk makes every lifted column zero and every character sum equal to `n`.
proof_steps.statement: Host-graph expansion and bounded walk length alone do not imply bias for an arbitrary sparse deterministic schedule.

research_direction: Spectral graph products and explicit bias reduction: deterministic explicitness equivalence for sparse mixed-parity lifts
theorem_statement: For the independently accepted rank-1040 RS–affine labeling, unrestricted sparse vertex-XOR walks and deterministic 1040-bit column streams are polynomial-time interconvertible: every column has a deterministic walk representation of at most 1040 visits with visit parity equal to its distinguished all-one coordinate, and every polynomial-total-visit walk stream yields the columns by XOR. A stream produces a `[2^30,1041,≥535822336]_2` all-one augmentation if and only if every nonzero character sum has magnitude at most `2^21`. Hence the sparse mixed-parity path format creates no explicitness shortcut: the missing object is still a symbolic Fourier-qualified column stream. No such stream is constructed here.
